b: When they said Mua Cave meant climbing a huge mountain, Mithra and I said we couldn't climb and all that and looked around down below.. The cave was down below… It's a small cave.. A terrific wind blows inside it… People who climb the mountain and come down sweating go in there and dry their shirts..While the others climbed and came back, we finished discussing the news of the town and the news of the world..
They showed us the photos they took, saying you can see really beautiful places if you climb up… Seeing them was enough, thank God, we said, and set off

Next, a boat trip on a river where the King Kong film was shot.. For three hours someone paddled on the river while we looked at the mountains, caves and temples all around…Sing Keeth, Mithra and I went in one boat, and Dhanush and Thushara went in another boat with another couple.. And Thushara fell asleep halfway

We took photos too and all our phones died… This was terribly beautiful too..Some people who saw us asked where we were from and we said Sri Lanka.. Oh, we know it, they said, and we were thrilled… Straight away they asked, you play football really well, don't you, and then we understood they thought it was Spain.. Embarrassing.. We laughed it off and came away..

At one point the woman rowing said King Kong, King Kong.. and we all took photos… Apparently that film was shot right here…It only became famous after that..Mithra was the one who'd been shouting she had to see this from the moment we arrived.. After seeing it, we too joined in the prayer for her soul's peace
Finally, when it was all over, the bus to our hotel came just in time.. We got on the bus and arrived back in Hanoi
note: The film is Kong: Skull Island (2017), parts of which were shot around Ninh Binh and Ha Long Bay.
